review.method: Encoded from the text of ss.107-108. The two sections are separate provisions, not subsections of one section: s.107 covers abetting the suicide of a child or a person with mental illness, a delirious person, or a person who is intoxicated (death, life, or up to ten years); s.108 covers abetting any other suicide (up to ten years). Neither punishment changed from the IPC (ss.305-306). 'Mental illness' is undefined in s.107 and is recorded as an unresolved ambiguity rather than guessed.

terms.definition: Instigates, conspires, or aids the suicide (BNS s.45). The encoding treats abetment as a single fact; which means of abetment is proved does not change the outcome.
A child, a person with mental illness, a delirious person, or an intoxicated person. Abetting their suicide is the separate offence in s.107, carrying death, life, or up to ten years.

branches.text: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide ...
branches.notes: No suicide means ss.107-108 are not engaged. Abetting an attempt is not this offence.

branches.text: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide ...
branches.notes: A suicide without abetment is not this offence. The abetment is the whole offence.

branches.text: If any child, any person with mental illness, any delirious person or any person who is intoxicated, commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
branches.notes: The vulnerable-victim offence. Re-enacts IPC s.305 with the same punishment.

branches.text: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
branches.notes: The general offence. Re-enacts IPC s.306 with the same punishment (up to ten years).

ambiguities.question: What counts as 'mental illness' in s.107?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Whether the victim had a mental illness decides between s.107 (death, life, or up to ten years) and s.108 (up to ten years). The section does not define the term, and the pack records only one reading, so the analyser reports n/a rather than a number.
ambiguities.position_a: Mental illness means a clinically recognised condition at the time of the suicide.
ambiguities.position_b: Mental illness includes any diagnosed or treated psychiatric condition, past or present.
